chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abdullah from Zurara ibn A'yan from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said:

Friday prayer is an obligation, and gathering for it with the Imam is an obligation. If a man abandons three Fridays without a reason, he has abandoned three obligations, and none abandons three obligations without a reason except a hypocrite.
And he (peace be upon him) said: Whoever abandons the congregational prayer out of aversion to it and to the Muslim congregation without a reason, then no prayer is [recorded] for him.

key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: The Imam — in early Shia jurisprudence, the just Imam whose presence or authorization legitimizes Friday prayer
key_terms.الْجَمَاعَةَ: Congregational prayer — the collective worship of the Muslim community
key_terms.صَلَاةُ الْجُمُعَةِ: Friday prayer — the obligatory congregational prayer performed at midday on Friday
key_terms.فَرِيضَةٌ: Religious obligation (farida) — a mandatory duty in Islamic law
key_terms.مُنَافِقٌ: Hypocrite (munafiq) — one who outwardly professes Islam while inwardly opposing it; abandoning communal obligations without cause is listed as its sign

ai.seo_question: Is Friday prayer (Jumu'a) obligatory in Shia Islam and what is the ruling for abandoning it?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) declares that the Friday prayer and its congregational gathering with the Imam are both obligatory acts. He then emphasizes the gravity of neglecting these duties by identifying habitual abandonment without valid excuse as a sign of hypocrisy. The ruling reflects the early Shia understanding of Friday prayer as a communal obligation tied to Imamic authority, addressed to the scholarly circle of Zurara ibn A'yan, one of the foremost jurists of the Imams.
